pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented from 00:29:15 and built directly on his fear — the shoulder named as the first thing to address, programmes tailored to limitations, 30 to 40 minute sessions starting nearer 20, and bespoke mobility protocols for hips and shoulder. He volunteered positive reactions throughout rather than just agreeing: "I remember reading that. I loved it. His entire philosophy is so sensible, I thought" on the six-month self-sufficiency model, and "I remember him saying in one of his videos that his desire is that we learn the craft, so we're able to teach our wives, our parents, our children, and everybody's just pain-free and healthy. Like, it's so clear this person cares about a movement." Asked whether it would work for him he said "Yeah. It makes me feel more relieved, as you might guess." He tied the pillar to his own goal unprompted and repeatedly, which is the enthusiastic marker. Worth noting the relief was produced by reassurance about pacing, not by any assessment of whether his shoulder can do the work.

Presented at 00:34:00 as the standard what/when/how-much model. He asked mechanical questions at three separate points: "The when with what windows, sorry?", "Andrew, what do you do when you get hungry outside of those eight hours?", and on the free meal "meal or one day?" He then positioned himself as experienced rather than needing convincing — "I have managed my nutrition before. So my discipline used to be great" and "Right now, I have an eight-hour window" — and reframed his own problem as psychological rather than informational: "When you're in pain and you're not able to do the stuff that you want to, I don't know if it's just like anger that comes out and you're just self-sabotaging." Clarifying rather than accepted, because he was working out the mechanics, and the substantive point he raised — that his lapse is emotional and tied to the injury — was acknowledged warmly but never addressed by the pillar.

Presented at 00:39:20 as the app, weekly check-ins, video form review and Trevor's cell number with an over-communication expectation. He responded "That's wonderful" and "it all sounds sensible", but his substantive engagement was a mechanics question: "The weekly check-in? Like, am I doing calls with Trevor every week to share an update, or am I just texting?" — answered as in-app, which he accepted ("that's perfect. That makes sense"). He then asked the sharper question of the call, which sits with this pillar because it is about whether the system works: "What has the success rate been like? Do you guys measure? And, you know, just what have the results been like?" That was declined as untrackable and answered with the guarantee instead. Recorded as clarifying: he wanted to understand and verify the delivery model, and on the verification half he did not get an answer.

anchors.raw: That's like, you know, six months of my rent, as an example. And so I, you know, I think about how much my wife and I, you know, we really reflected on, are we going to be able to afford the place we've got for rent?
anchors.note: The reference point is not a competing product, it is his housing cost — the strongest form of the affordability anchor because it makes $6,000 a lifestyle decision rather than a purchase. It also came with a precedent attached: he and his wife had already had a hard deliberation about affording the rent itself. Nothing in the call attempted to change the comparison set.

anchors.raw: 7,800. So that's like 30% a year. Okay, I've understood.
anchors.competitor: Payva (positioned by the rep against Klarna)
anchors.note: Introduced by the rep as the solution to the affordability objection and it functioned as the opposite. Within two minutes of the number appearing the prospect went from engaged to "I'm just a little overwhelmed right now" and "All of this is more than naturally strikes me as comfortable." A financing option that adds roughly $1,800 to a price already anchored against six months of rent moved the deal backwards, and it was offered instead of answering his direct question about a $1,000-a-month in-house plan. See the flags file.

anchors.raw: the exercise programs that they've suggested to help me prevent the same issues cropping up again, it's just not helped me, you know, so I've got this. Same issue now for the last year, year and a half
anchors.note: He has already paid professionals for this exact problem and got pain relief but no resolution. That cuts both ways — it creates the need, but it also establishes a personal precedent that paying an expert for this does not fix it. The rep leaned entirely on the first half and never addressed the second, which is also why this anchor produced a clinical exposure rather than a commercial one.

anchors.raw: I showed her the program to ask her what she thinks, because her BS detector with these things is way stronger than mine is, and she seemed to think this was good and legit, so I do have her blessing with this
anchors.note: Unusually strong. The spouse is a professional fitness and nutrition coach, was shown the material specifically as a credibility check, and passed it. The rep did probe the obvious substitute — "since your wife is into fitness, haven't you thought about her coaching you on fitness?" — and the prospect dismissed it himself: "When your wife does it, she's not able to be as strict with me as she is with her clients." So the nearest free alternative was raised and closed by the prospect, unprompted. This anchor was surfaced and then barely used in the OB play that followed.

anchors.raw: I'm sure I'll do well enough on my own, but if someone's gone through the journey and can help me get there in a better way, faster way, maybe even further, because otherwise I'm probably not going to train with kettlebells and, you know, things like that out of fear
anchors.note: He is already training three to five times a week, walking 10-20k steps a day and reports it going well — "it's felt good. I am progressing." He states plainly that he expects to do well enough alone. He also states the one thing he will not do alone, which is kettlebells, out of fear. That sentence contains the entire commercial case for the programme and the rep never returned to it.

anchors.raw: there's a guarantee. I don't think there's another program. Out there that the trainer puts a guarantee, and the guarantee is that in six months, you're gonna add eight kilos to your baseline kettlebell
anchors.note: Deployed as the substitute for the outcome data he asked for. He accepted it as evidence of good faith — "there's a guarantee associated with it. I've seen Trevor's videos, so I believe that that must be the case" — so it worked as a trust signal. It is worth noting for the rollup that the guarantee metric is added kettlebell load while this prospect's stated goal is to train without being injured, and his wrist has already been hurt by kettlebell work. The guarantee is denominated in the thing he is afraid of.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded kettlebell work is safe for a right shoulder that eighteen months of physiotherapy has not resolved, and for a left wrist that his own previous kettlebell attempts injured.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer answered a clinical question with programme design and reassurance — tailoring, slower ramp, a first month of movement learning. No clinician clearance was sought or suggested, his imaging and reports were referenced but never asked for ("I'd have to check what the reports say"), and nobody proposed involving the physiotherapist who is already treating him. The one thing that would actually resolve this want sits outside the product entirely and was never named.

unmet_demand.want: To start at roughly one session a week and build from there, beginning with a narrow set of stabilising movements — rotations, dead hangs, swings, Turkish get-ups — while continuing his gym work.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked for this explicitly and in detail: "I probably want to start with even like one day a week, just to check what am I feeling like the next day" and "I would be okay, even with starting with just that, with the gym work." The rep answered with the standard three to four sessions a week and a first month of movement learning, which is adjacent but not the same thing, and never confirmed whether a one-day-a-week start or continuing his gym programme alongside is permitted. Almost certainly accommodatable by a tailored programme; nobody said so.

unmet_demand.want: Outcome data — measured success rates, results, and dropout or completion figures.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked directly and clearly: "What has the success rate been like? Do you guys measure? ... if there's anything you guys track." The answer was that it is "difficult to track a success rate because it's a very, I would say, kind of a vague thing to track", followed by a pivot to the guarantee. Whether such data exists internally cannot be determined from this call, and a prospect asking a reasonable diligence question about a $6,000 purchase received no figure of any kind.

unmet_demand.want: Level monthly payments at face value for cash-flow reasons — specifically the six-by-$1,000 structure he asked the rep to confirm.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He stated the preference generally ("In general, with everything that I do, I prefer monthly payments to lump sum. It helps from a cash flow perspective tremendously") and then asked precisely: "what you guys can do is break it into six payments at 1k a month. Did I understand that correctly? Like that's what you guys can do from your side?" The question was never answered. He was routed to third-party financing at roughly 30 percent instead, even though the same rep offered another prospect an explicitly interest-free in-house split two days earlier. This is a positioning and consistency failure rather than a missing capability.

unmet_demand.want: Help with the emotional and self-sabotage component of losing discipline while injured, rather than with nutritional information he already has.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He diagnosed it himself — "my discipline used to be great... When you're in pain and you're not able to do the stuff that you want to, I don't know if it's just like anger that comes out and you're just self-sabotaging." The nutrition pillar answers what, when and how much, and the accountability pillar answers check-ins and messaging. Neither addresses behaviour under pain and frustration, which he identifies as the actual mechanism of his decline. Nothing false was said; nothing was offered either.
